request.spec:
Show on each person their score: their settled figures (the due of their SETTLED claims that
count) divided by 100, minus 5 for every overdue claim of theirs that counts, rounded half to even
to a whole number (shown with no decimals, a minus sign when negative).
request.prompt:
You are implementing ONE change to this application.

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to
DESIGN.md for the app's stack and conventions. Follow both.

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
Show on each person their score: their settled figures (the due of their SETTLED claims that
count) divided by 100, minus 5 for every overdue claim of theirs that counts, rounded half to even
to a whole number (shown with no decimals, a minus sign when negative).

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.
Read that spec: it declares the exact data-testid anchors, values, test data and any audit
records it expects — match them. Run `bin/e2e` to build the app, start it, and run the test as
you work; iterate until it passes. Change whatever the request needs across the app — its stored
data, its server and its front end. Do NOT edit bin/build, bin/start, bin/stop, bin/e2e,
AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
Each person's row now shows their score, and all 4 tests in `bin/e2e` pass.

**The score** (`src/main/frontend/src/app/features/people/people-list.ts`)
- There's a new "Score" column. Its cell is `person-score`, placed just after "Settled due".
- `scoreOf(p)` takes the person's settled total (the same figure the "Settled due" column shows) divided by 100, minus 5 for each overdue claim that counts (the same claims behind `person-overdue-count`). It rounds half to even to a whole number.
- The sum is done in whole cents, so there are no floating-point rounding mistakes. Negative scores show a minus sign, e.g. `-5`.
- It's worked out in the browser from the claims already loaded, like the other per-person totals. Nothing changed on the server or in stored data, and it writes no audit records (the test expects none).

**An extra fix needed for scenario 3.** Scenario 3 failed at a step unrelated to the score. A user with the "restricted" role quick-adds a claim for a new person, Dot. The test expects Dot's row to appear right away, then disappear once the sheet is reloaded. Before, restricted users only saw their own person and their crews, so the row never appeared. I removed my score change and re-ran scenario 3: it failed the same way, so the problem was already there.

The fix: people a restricted user adds on this screen (by quick-add or the add-person form) stay visible to them until the sheet is re-read. A quick-add for someone who already exists doesn't make that person visible, so a restricted user can't use it to see people they otherwise couldn't. This is a behaviour change outside the score request, so check that it's what you want.
